rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording ‘they glorify Him’ with ‘for Him’ rather than a direct object restricts their glorification to God alone.
rows.anchor: وقوله { يسبحون له } ولم يقل يسبحونه للدلالة على الحصر والاختصاص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If disbelievers refuse to prostrate to God alone, His worship still continues through constant angelic glorification.
rows.anchor: فإن استكبر هؤلاء الكفار عن السجدة لله وحده فعبادته تعالى لا ترتفع من الوجود فهناك من يسبحه تسبيحا دائما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘By night and day’ means without interruption; angels have no night or day and never tire of glorifying God.
rows.anchor: وقوله { بالليل والنهار } أي دائما لا ينقطع فإن الملائكة ليس عندهم ليل ولا نهار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khushūʿ is humility, ihtizāz is intense movement, and rubū is growth, flourishing, and rising.
rows.anchor: الخشوع التذلل، والاهتزاز التحرك الشديد،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The earth’s shaking and rising describe its plants moving and growing upward.
rows.anchor: واهتزاز الأرض وربوها تحركها بنباتها وارتفاعه

words: خَاشِعَةً فَإِذَا أَنزَلْنَا عَلَيْهَا ٱلْمَاءَ ٱهْتَزَّتْ وَرَبَتْ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A representative metaphor compares barren earth turning green to a poor, shabby person transformed by wealth into a splendid, lively figure.
rows.anchor: وفي الآية استعارة تمثيلية شبهت فيها الأرض في جدبها وخلوها عن النبات ثم اخضرارها ونمو نباتها وعلوه بشخص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The earth’s revival argues for resurrection; al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī says this argument was discussed in earlier sūras.
rows.anchor: والآية مسوقة للاحتجاج على المعاد

rows.speaker: علي عليه السلام
rows.claim: A report from ʿAlī identifies the two who led people astray as Iblīs and Cain, the first to introduce disobedience.
rows.anchor: وروى ذلك عن علي عليه السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī considers that identification an instance of applying a general verse (jary).
rows.anchor: أقول ولعله من نوع الجري فالآية عامة

rows.speaker: مجاهد والسدي وأبو عبد الله عليه السلام
rows.claim: Mujāhid and al-Suddī, and a report from Abū ʿAbd Allāh, explain the angels’ descent as occurring at death.
rows.anchor: يعني عند الموت عن مجاهد والسدي وروي ذلك عن أبي عبد الله عليه السلام

rows.speaker: القمي
rows.claim: Al-Qummī explains the angels’ worldly guardianship as protection from devils and their next-life guardianship as occurring at death.
rows.anchor: وفي تفسير القمي في قوله تعالى { نحن أولياؤكم في الحياة الدنيا } قال كنا نحرسكم من الشياطين

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A report in al-Majmaʿ says the angels guard believers in this life and at death, the beginning of the hereafter.
rows.anchor: وفي المجمع في الآية قيل { نحن أولياؤكم في الحياة الدنيا } أي نحرسكم في الدنيا وعند الموت في الآخرة

rows.speaker: القمي
rows.claim: Al-Qummī says to answer an offender’s bad act with good treatment until the former enemy becomes like a close friend.
rows.anchor: وفي تفسير القمي في قوله تعالى { ادفع بالتي هي أحسن } قال ادفع سيئة من أساء إليك بحسنتك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This passage identifies revelation by its content: the one divine religion, a way of life people should follow toward happiness.
rows.anchor: يعرف الوحي الإلهي بأثره الذي هو مفاده وما احتوى عليه من المضمون وهو الدين الإلهي الواحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The context presents Muḥammad’s law as encompassing revealed laws, while divisions arise from human transgression after knowledge, not revelation.
rows.anchor: الشريعة المحمدية أجمع الشرائع المنزلة وأن الاختلافات الواقعة في دين الله على وحدته ليست من ناحية الوحي السماوي وإنما هي من بغي الناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb sharaʿa, as in ‘he made a road,’ means to make a clear, level path.
rows.anchor: يقال شرع الطريق شرعا أي سواه طريقا واضحا بينا

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Al-Rāghib defines a testament as urging another to act with admonition; the related expression for land describes continuous vegetation.
rows.anchor: قال الراغب الوصية التقدم إلى الغير بما يعمل مقترنا بوعظ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The choice of ‘enjoined’ signals special importance, since one selects matters about which one particularly cares.
rows.anchor: وفي معناه إشعار بالأهمية فما كل أمر يوصى به

words: شَرَعَ لَكُم مِّنَ ٱلدِّينِ مَا وَصَّىٰ بِهِۦ نُوحًا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God clarified for the Prophet and his community a religious way of life, including the law entrusted to Noah; the address includes both.
rows.anchor: أي بين وأوضح لكم من الدين وهو سنة الحياة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The contrast with Noah points to the knowledge and rulings distinctive to Muḥammad’s law; his comprehensive law includes major and minor matters unlike earlier, more limited laws.
rows.anchor: ظاهر المقابلة بينه وبين نوح عليه السلام أن المراد بما أوحى إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The shift to first-person plural in ‘what We revealed’ conveys majesty, as dignitaries speak for themselves and their attendants.
rows.anchor: والالتفات في قوله { والذي أوحينا } من الغيبة إلى التكلم

words: وَمَا وَصَّيْنَا بِهِۦٓ إِبْرَٰهِيمَ وَمُوسَىٰ وَعِيسَىٰٓ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase is coordinated with the clause about Noah and means the law prescribed for each of Abraham, Moses, and Jesus.
rows.anchor: وقوله { وما وصينا به إبراهيم وموسى وعيسى } عطف على قوله { وما وصى به }

words: نُوحًا وَٱلَّذِىٓ أَوْحَيْنَآ إِلَيْكَ وَمَا وَصَّيْنَا بِهِۦٓ إِبْرَٰهِيمَ وَمُوسَىٰ وَعِيسَىٰٓ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lawgivers are otherwise named chronologically; Muḥammad is placed first to honor and privilege him.
rows.anchor: وإنما قدم ذكر النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم للتشريف والتفضيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cited covenant verse likewise places Muḥammad before Noah, Abraham, Moses, and Jesus.
rows.anchor: وإذ أخذنا من النبيين ميثاقهم ومنك ومن نوح وإبراهيم وموسى وعيسى ابن مريم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Noah is named first to indicate the antiquity and long duration of this law.
rows.anchor: وإنما قدم نوحا وبدأ به للدلالة على قدم هذه الشريعة وطول عهدها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The tone of divine favor, especially the verse’s ending and next verse, indicates that Muḥammad’s law encompasses earlier laws.
rows.anchor: أن السياق بما أنه يفيد الامتنان وخاصة بالنظر إلى ذيل الآية والآية التالية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Each community having its own law and path does not rule out a law’s comprehensiveness.
rows.anchor: لكل جعلنا منكم شرعة ومنهاجا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The divinely revealed laws are those of Noah, Abraham, Moses, Jesus, and Muḥammad; the verse would name any others.
rows.anchor: الشرائع الإلهية المنتسبة إلى الوحي إنما هي شريعة نوح وإبراهيم وموسى وعيسى ومحمد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This entails that before Noah there was no social law in the sense of rules governing communities and resolving social conflict.
rows.anchor: أن لا شريعة قبل نوح عليه السلام بمعنى القوانين الحاكمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Prophets after Noah followed Noah’s law until Abraham; later prophets followed Abraham’s law until Moses, and so on.
rows.anchor: أن الأنبياء المبعوثين بعد نوح كانوا على شريعته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The five named prophets are the law-bearing, resolute prophets; the verse would have named any others.
rows.anchor: الأنبياء أصحاب الشرائع وأولي العزم هم هؤلاء الخمسة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The particle an introduces an explanation of the preceding command to prescribe religion.
rows.anchor: أن تفسيرية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Establishing religion means preserving it through adherence and practice; the definite article refers to this prescribed religion, and avoiding division preserves its unity.
rows.anchor: إقامة الدين حفظه بالاتباع والعمل

words: أَنْ أَقِيمُوا۟ ٱلدِّينَ وَلَا تَتَفَرَّقُوا۟ فِيهِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Everyone must uphold the whole revealed religion together, without fragmenting it by observing some parts and abandoning others.
rows.anchor: محصله أن عليهم جميعا إقامة الدين جميعا وعدم التفرق والتشتت فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: All revealed laws are one religion that people must establish without division, believing everything revealed and practicing what is binding.
rows.anchor: فجميع الشرائع التي أنزلها الله على أنبيائه دين واحد يجب إقامته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An abrogated ruling remains true for its particular people and period; abrogation discloses its end rather than invalidating it.
rows.anchor: فالحكم المنسوخ حق دائما غير أنه خاص بطائفة خاصة في زمن خاص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People living under a ruling must believe and practice it; later people must believe it was true without practicing it after its term ends.
rows.anchor: يجب عليهم أن يؤمنوا به ويعملوا به

words: أَنْ أَقِيمُوا۟ ٱلدِّينَ وَلَا تَتَفَرَّقُوا۟ فِيهِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command is unrestricted and applies to everyone in every age.
rows.anchor: مطلق شامل لجميع الناس في جميع الأزمان

rows.speaker: جمع
rows.claim: Some restrict the command to rulings shared by revealed laws, treating law-specific rules as varying by community; al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī rejects this limitation.
rows.anchor: فساد قول جمع إن الأمر بالإقامة وعدم التفرق إنما يشمل الأحكام المشتركة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: That restriction would reduce the command to the three fundamentals, since no detailed rule is common in every respect across all laws; this conflicts with the context and cited verses.
rows.anchor: ولو كان كما يقولون كان الأمر بالإقامة مختصا بأصول الدين الثلاثة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: What the Prophet calls the polytheists to is the religion of divine unity, not merely the bare principle of God’s oneness.
rows.anchor: المراد بقوله { ما تدعوهم إليه } دين التوحيد الذي كان يدعو إليه النبي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The religion’s being burdensome to the polytheists means that they are reluctant to accept it.
rows.anchor: والمراد بكبره على المشركين تحرجهم من قبوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ijtibāʾ means to gather and draw someone near.
rows.anchor: الاجتباء هو الجمع والاجتلاب

words: ٱللَّهُ يَجْتَبِىٓ إِلَيْهِ مَن يَشَآءُ وَيَهْدِىٓ إِلَيْهِ مَن يُنِيبُ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronouns in ‘to it’ share an antecedent: the religion of divine unity, to which God draws whom He wills and guides whoever turns to Him.
rows.anchor: ومقتضى اتساق الضمائر أن يكون ضمير { إليه } الثاني والثالث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase echoes God’s choosing Abraham’s community and relieving it of hardship.
rows.anchor: هو اجتباكم وما جعل عليكم في الدين من حرج ملة أبيكم إبراهيم

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another possible reading takes the pronouns as referring to God; al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī says the contextual reading is more fitting.
rows.anchor: وقيل الضميران لله تعالى، ولا بأس به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s choosing and guiding whom He wills makes the faith of the arrogant polytheists unnecessary, as when disbelievers are contrasted with the angels’ worship.
rows.anchor: قوله { الله يجتبي إليه } إلى آخر الآية موضوع موضع الاستغناء

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view says the call is to belief in the Messenger and that his message troubled them; the author calls this contrary to the apparent sense.
rows.anchor: وقيل المراد بما تدعوهم إليه ما تدعوهم إلى الإيمان به وهو الرسالة

words: وَمَا تَفَرَّقُوا۟ إِلَّا مِنۢ بَعْدِ مَا جَآءَهُمُ ٱلْعِلْمُ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The subject of ‘they divided’ is the people understood from context; baghy means injustice or envy, and ‘among themselves’ signals its circulation.
rows.anchor: ضمير { تفرقوا } للناس المفهوم من السياق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People divided over revealed law after learning the truth, out of injustice or envy passed among them; religious disagreement produces sects and factions attributed to transgression.
rows.anchor: وهذا هو الاختلاف في الدين المؤدي إلى الانشعابات والتحزبات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Social and economic differences arise from varying human aims and prompt revelation of law to resolve them, unlike blameworthy religious division.
rows.anchor: وأما الاختلاف المؤدي إلى نزول الشريعة وهو الاختلاف في شؤون الحياة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prior decree is that people may settle and enjoy the earth until an appointed time.
rows.anchor: المراد بالكلمة مثل قوله حين إهباط آدم عليه السلام إلى الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Without that appointed term, God would have judged and destroyed them immediately for dividing over religion and straying from His path.
rows.anchor: لقضي بينهم إثر تفرقهم في دينه وانحرافهم عن سبيله

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some grammarians allow the clause to coordinate with a conditional apodosis by supplying an implicit an and putting the verb in the subjunctive; al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī notes the syntax is disputed.
rows.anchor: وجوز بعضهم أن يكون معطوفا على جزاء الشرط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse divides provision into worldly goods shared by believers and unbelievers and afterlife reward for believers, then turns to believers’ qualities and wrongdoers’ fate.
rows.anchor: تفصيل لما تقدم ذكره من الرزق وتقسيم له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The address is to people generally, and ‘whatever you have been given’ includes all blessings and provision they receive.
rows.anchor: الخطاب للناس على ما يفيده السياق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling it worldly enjoyment signals its short duration and lack of permanence: people enjoy it only for a few days.
rows.anchor: وإضافة المتاع إلى الحياة للإشارة إلى انقطاعه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: What God has is the reward He stored to repay believers.
rows.anchor: ما ادخره الله ثوابا ليثيب به المؤمنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lām is possessive and the adverbial phrase is loose; another analysis connects the lām to ‘more lasting,’ but the first is clearer.
rows.anchor: واللام في { للذين آمنوا } للملك والظرف لغو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reward is better because it is free of pain and distress, and more lasting because it never ends.
rows.anchor: وكون ما عند الله خيرا لكونه خالصا من الألم والكدر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This clause is coordinated with ‘those who believe’; it and the next two verses list believers’ qualities, while an independent start does not fit the context.
rows.anchor: عطف على قوله { الذين آمنوا } والآية وآيتان بعدها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Major sins have grave harmful consequences; the Qur’an counts wine and gambling among them.
rows.anchor: وكبائر الإثم المعاصي الكبيرة التي لها آثار سوء عظيمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fawāḥish are atrocious, indecent sins; God counts adultery and same-sex intercourse among them, citing adultery as a flagrant indecency.
rows.anchor: والفواحش جمع فاحشة وهي المعصية الشنيعة النكراء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rhetorical question asks whether God would turn the Qur’anic reminder away because they are excessive; the implied answer is no.
rows.anchor: والمعنى أفنصرف عنكم الذكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase can also mean turning the reminder aside because of their excess; al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī again denies that God would do so.
rows.anchor: أو أفنصرفه عنكم إلى جانب لكونكم مسرفين

words: وَكَمْ أَرْسَلْنَا مِن نَّبِىٍّ فِى الْأَوَّلِينَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kam expresses abundance; ‘the earlier ones’ are past nations, and the clause about mockery is circumstantial, governed by ‘We sent.’
rows.anchor: والأولون هم الأمم الدارجة و { ما يأتيهم }

words: وَمَا يَأْتِيهِم مِّن نَّبِىٍّ إِلَّا كَانُوا۟ بِهِۦ يَسْتَهْزِءُونَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Past prophets were sent despite mockery and the mockers were destroyed; the current people’s excess likewise brings destruction rather than withdrawal of revelation, promising the Prophet and warning his people.
rows.anchor: فإنا كثيرا ما أرسلنا من نبي في الأمم الماضين

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Al-Rāghib defines baṭsh as seizing something forcefully.
rows.anchor: قال الراغب البطش تناول الشيء بصولة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The shift in ‘than them’ from direct address to speaking of them turns to the Prophet because they do not learn from these accounts and prepares the reference to the past.
rows.anchor: وفي الآية التفات في قوله { منهم } من الخطاب إلى الغيبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Earlier sūras described former nations and how what they mocked came upon them.
rows.anchor: ومضى في السور النازلة قبل هذه السورة من القرآن وصف الأمم الأولين

words: وَلَئِن سَأَلْتَهُم مَّنْ خَلَقَ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلْأَرْضَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Verses 9–14 argue that God alone is Lord: the polytheists admit He created all, while His acts of creation also govern human needs; they otherwise assign governance to others.
rows.anchor: في الآية وما يتلوها إلى تمام ست آيات احتجاج على ربوبيته تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God made the earth a place where people are nurtured, as children are raised in a cradle.
rows.anchor: أي جعل لكم الأرض بحيث تربون فيها كما يربى الأطفال في المهد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God placed roads in the earth for people to travel and find their destinations.
rows.anchor: وجعل لكم في الأرض سبلا وطرقا تسلكونها

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: An alternative takes ‘so that you may be guided’ to mean guidance to knowledge of God and worshipping Him alone; the author prefers guidance along roads.
rows.anchor: وقيل معنى { لعلكم تهتدون } رجاء أن تهتدوا إلى معرفة الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The shift to address the people emphasizes that governance belongs with creation; admitting God alone creates while others govern is incoherent, and direct address rebukes them.
rows.anchor: وفي الكلام التفات إلى خطاب القوم بعد صرف الخطاب عنهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rain is measured to show that it comes through intention and governance, not by chance.
rows.anchor: قيد تنزيل الماء بقدر للإشارة إلى أنه عن إرادة وتدبير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Anshara means to bring to life; mayyit is the lighter form of the intensified mayyit, and a town is described as dead because it is a place.
rows.anchor: والميت مخفف الميت بالتشديد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The shift to first-person plural in ‘We revived’ signals special attention.
rows.anchor: والالتفات عن الغيبة إلى التكلم مع الغير في { أنشرنا }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Measured rain and revival show God’s creation and governance, from which the verse infers resurrection: people will be raised alive from their graves as the dead land was revived.
rows.anchor: ولما استدل بتنزيل الماء بقدر وإحياء البلدة الميتة على خلقه وتدبيره

words: فَأَنشَرْنَا بِهِۦ بَلْدَةًۭ مَّيْتًۭا كَذَٰلِكَ تُخْرَجُونَ
rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One explanation says describing plants as revived and people as brought forth magnifies plant growth and makes resurrection seem easy, clarifying the analogy.
rows.anchor: قيل في التعبير عن إخراج النبات بالانشار الذي هو إحياء الموتى

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One view takes ‘all pairs’ to mean kinds of beings, including male and female, white and black, and others.
rows.anchor: قيل المراد بالأزواج أصناف الموجودات من ذكر وأنثى

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view takes it as pairs of every thing apart from God, such as above/below, right/left, and male/female.
rows.anchor: وقيل المراد الزوج من كل شيء فكل ما سوى الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘What you ride’ means what you ride upon; the verb takes a direct object for animals but takes fī with ships, so the wording favors the animal construction.
rows.anchor: والركوب إذا نسب إلى الحيوان كالفرس والإبل تعدى بنفسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Istiwāʾ on the backs means settling on them, and both pronouns refer to ‘what you ride.’
rows.anchor: الاستواء على الظهور الاستقرار عليها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The blessing recalled after mounting is the utility of God’s subjection of ships and animals, such as travel and carrying loads.
rows.anchor: ذكر النعم التي ينتفع بها الإنسان بتسخيره تعالى له هذه المراكب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another possible sense is to recall God’s blessings generally, moving from mention of vehicle blessings to God Himself.
rows.anchor: أو المراد ذكر مطلق نعمه تعالى بالانتقال من ذكر هذه النعم إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Remembering a blessing when using it ordinarily means thanking its giver; that gratitude differs from the following glorification.
rows.anchor: وظاهر ذكر النعمة عند استعمالها والانتفاع بها شكر منعمها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The utterance glorifies God as transcendent from anything unworthy of His majesty, especially a partner in lordship or divinity; it is not itself thanks.
rows.anchor: فإن هذا القول تسبيح وتنزيه له عما لا يليق بساحة كبريائه

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم وأئمة أهل البيت عليهم السلام
rows.claim: Reports from the Prophet and Imams about what to say when mounting vary, but include praise in addition to glorification.
rows.anchor: ما ورد عن النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم وأئمة أهل البيت عليهم السلام في ما يقال عند الاستواء على المركوب

rows.speaker: الحسن بن علي عليهما السلام
rows.claim: Al-Kashshāf reports that al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī asked a man who said the riding glorification whether he had been commanded to say it.
rows.anchor: وروى في الكشاف عن الحسن بن علي عليهما السلام أنه رأى رجلا يركب دابة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muqrinīn means capable or able; iqrān means ability.
rows.anchor: أي مطيقين والإقران الإطاقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The declaration that they will return to their Lord affirms resurrection.
rows.anchor: أي صائرون شهادة بالمعاد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God did not will by creative decree to prevent their worship of partners, so they remained free rather than compelled; by legislative will He commanded worship of Him alone.
rows.anchor: فهو سبحانه لما لم يشأ أن لا يعبدوا الشركاء بالإرادة التكوينية كانوا مختارين غير مضطرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Legislative will can be disobeyed because it is a conventional directive rather than a creative act; it operates in laws and obligations and rests on an act’s benefit or harm.
rows.anchor: والإرادة التشريعية لا يستحيل تخلف المراد عنها

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One argument says God willed the pagans’ angel worship and that this made it pleasing to Him; al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī accepts the first premise but rejects the second.
rows.anchor: فساد ما قيل إن حجتهم مبنية على مقدمتين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Failure to will that they abandon worship does not entail willing that they perform it; it entails only permission or not preventing the act.
rows.anchor: عدم تعلق المشيئة بالترك لا يستلزم تعلق المشيئة بالفعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The alternative argument wrongly ignores legislative will, which underlies religious commands and obligations.
rows.anchor: قصر الإرادة في التكوينية وإهمال التشريعية التي عليها المدار

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some say the pagans excused worship while admitting it was wrong; al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī rejects this because they did not concede its wrongness and instead cite ancestral custom.
rows.anchor: ما نسب إلى بعضهم أن المراد بقولهم { لو شاء الرحمن ما عبدناهم } الاعتذار

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Al-Rāghib takes kharṣ to mean speaking from conjecture and estimation; it is also explained as lying.
rows.anchor: على ما يظهر من الراغب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse denies scriptural proof, just as the preceding verse denied rational proof; they have no warrant for angel worship and God did not authorize it.
rows.anchor: وفي الآية نفي أن يكون لهم حجة من طريق النقل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ummah means a way or course that is intended and followed, and here it means religion.
rows.anchor: الأمة الطريقة التي تؤم وتقصد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bal turns from the preceding findings: the pagans have no evidence for their worship but rely on imitating their fathers’ religion.
rows.anchor: والإضراب عما تحصل من الآيتين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ancestral imitation also marked earlier polytheist communities: their affluent leaders answered each warner by citing their forefathers’ religion and refusing to abandon it.
rows.anchor: أي إن التشبث بذيل التقليد ليس مما يختص بهؤلاء
